claims.text: MLIPs trained on ab initio data can attain accuracy near that of the underlying DFT calculations.
Active learning can tailor an MLIP training set to a selected class of systems and properties while minimizing the required DFT calculations.
An actively learned MLIP can accurately reproduce ab initio free energies for both solid and liquid states across fusion.
The MLIP can retain the full vibrational-entropy contribution to the phase free energies.
Sparse ab initio MD configurations sampled from 0.8 to 1.2 times the melting temperature are sufficient training data for the proposed MLIP.
Atomic short-range order and vibrational-displacement distributions extracted from ab initio MD provide an effective structural mediator for learning fusion thermodynamics.
Active learning will identify and emphasize rare anharmonic configurations near the fusion point.
Active learning of atomic configurations enables the MLIP to capture electron-vibration coupling effects.
Capturing rare anharmonic events and electron-vibration coupling enables reproduction of the full free-energy landscape across fusion.
The MLIP will reduce computational cost relative to explicit ab initio MD.
The proposed workflow will be 10 to 100 times faster than full ab initio MD.
The workflow will match or surpass TOR-TILD performance for elemental and binary systems.
The workflow will maintain high fidelity for free energies, fusion temperatures, and latent heats.
The proposed validated domain is elemental and binary metals, including Al or Ni, from approximately 0.8 to 1.2 times their melting temperatures.
MLIP accuracy may degrade for configurations not adequately represented in the training set.
Generalization of the proposed fusion workflow to multicomponent high-entropy systems remains unvalidated.
